The selected F140 and EF98 caller windows reload the same current index at r1+0x12CC and materialize their r3 receivers from [0x8314F300].
The raw D1FC/D208 windows corroborate the increment slot and the unsigned +0x420C incoming-object bound test.

conclusion: The generated F140 and EF98 interior windows have the same explicit write footprint: for receiver R=r3 and index i=r4, they write 4 bytes at R+0x48C+0x18*i, 4 bytes at R+0x490+0x18*i, write the +0x10 word a second time, and OR an 8-byte dirty mask at R+0x18. The selected callers materialize R from [0x8314F300] and i from [r1+0x12CC]. Under the retained normal-return loop and the incoming-object +0x420C test, i is 0..3 or 0..7, so these explicit stores are outside same-base device float shadows D+0x780..D+0xD7F and D+0x1780..D+0x17FF; arbitrary computed indices can overlap those ranges at VS i=32..95 or PS i=202..207. The generated interior windows contain no explicit r1-based data store, so excluding staged-stack alteration by those stores requires the explicit interval condition for R and S=r1; a receiver/frame alias could overwrite them. ABI save/restore helpers and unexpanded callee 0x827F7C8C may have additional frame or memory effects and remain unresolved. This is a conditional explicit-store footprint and noninterference result, not a complete-body, draw, cadence, lifetime, restore, or safe constant-reuse proof.
